latest_release.name: Savage Wind 0.5.3 (0.5.3-alpha.5)
latest_release.body:
**Savage Wind 0.5.3: quick fixes.**

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **No game files are included.** You need your own legally obtained copy of the game, updated to **version 1.9.0**
> (and the DLC, version 3.0, if you want it), extracted from **your own** Nintendo Switch. Savage Wind provides no game
> files, keys, firmware, dumping or decryption tools, or instructions to obtain any of them, and it never decrypts
> anything. The game code is recompiled on your machine, from your files, for your own use only: don't share it.
> Respect the copyright laws of your country. This is a fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo.

## Downloads

| File | For | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `SavageWind-0.5.3-alpha.5-windows.zip` | Windows 10 or later, x86-64 | Supported |
| `Savage_Wind-0.5.3-alpha.5-x86_64.AppImage` | Linux x86-64 with glibc 2.35 or newer (Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12, Fedora 36, Arch, SteamOS...) | Supported |
| `Savage_Wind-0.5.3-alpha.5-aarch64.AppImage` | Linux on ARM64 with a Vulkan 1.3 driver | **Highly experimental** |

The `.sig` files next to them are what Savage Wind checks before it installs an update: you don't need them.

## Updating to 0.5.3

**From 0.5.1 or 0.5.2:** Savage Wind Configuration offers it: press **Update**. Your game files, saves and settings stay.

**From 0.5.0 or older:** by hand, once: extract the zip over your old folder (Windows), or use the new AppImage (Linux).

**Stuck at 99% right now:** close Savage Wind (with Task Manager if it doesn't close), then extract the 0.5.3 zip over
your Savage Wind folder and start it again.

## Fixes

- **Setup stuck at 99%** while precompiling shaders, on AMD cards with Windows after updating to 0.5.2 (21502 of 21503
  pipelines), where Esc could not stop it either ([#359](https://github.com/Revivedx/SavageWindRecomp/issues/359)). A
  shader compile the graphics driver never finishes no longer holds setup up: after 3 minutes without progress, or when
  you press Esc, setup goes on without it, and `savagewind.log` names the shader.
- **Rain and torch particles** stretched across the screen for a frame
  ([#620](https://github.com/Revivedx/SavageWindRecomp/issues/620), [#629](https://github.com/Revivedx/SavageWindRecomp/issues/629),
  [#683](https://github.com/Revivedx/SavageWindRecomp/issues/683), [#717](https://github.com/Revivedx/SavageWindRecomp/issues/717)).
  If you set `SAVAGEWIND_GPU_OVERLAP=0` for this, please remove it: it costs a lot of frame rate, and the fix costs
  about 1%.

## Still open

The **black, dark or wrong sky on AMD cards with Windows** (RX 6000 and older) is not fixed: the 0.5.2 change did not do
it. If you have it, please follow the steps on [#359](https://github.com/Revivedx/SavageWindRecomp/issues/359).

## Found a bug?

Open a [bug report](https://github.com/Revivedx/SavageWindRecomp/issues/new/choose) with `savagewind.log`, or make one zip with **Options > Problem report**. If an update fails, `SW Update.log` in the Savage Wind folder says why.

## Thanks

To everyone who reported these with logs, videos and tests, so quickly.

This release was made almost entirely with AI (Anthropic's Claude, through Claude Code), directed, tested and
reviewed by a human.

detail.readme:
Download · Get started · Status · FAQ · Issues · Changelog

**Savage Wind Recomp** is a work-in-progress static recompilation of *The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild* (Nintendo Switch, version 1.9.0) into a native application for Windows and Linux, built from your own copy of the game.

Screenshots taken in Savage Wind. The game is © Nintendo; you need your own copy to run it.

> [!IMPORTANT] > **No game files are included.** You need your own legally obtained copy of the game, updated to **version 1.9.0** > and dumped from **your own** Nintendo Switch. This project does not provide game files, keys, firmware, dumping or > decryption tools, or instructions on how to obtain them. The game code is recompiled locally, on your machine, > from your files. > [!NOTE] > **Made almost entirely with AI.** Nearly all of the code, tooling, reverse engineering and documentation is written > by an AI (Anthropic's Claude, through Claude Code), directed, tested and reviewed by a human. It builds on > [LAS Recomp](https://github.com/peiikai/LASRecomp), made the same way. If you don't trust code written by AI, you > can simply ignore this project. > [!WARNING] > **This is an alpha.** The whole game can be finished from start to end, but expect bugs and crashes in some places, > and some mechanics that break above 30 fps ([#425](https://github.com/Revivedx/SavageWindRecomp/issues/425)). If a > cutscene freezes or breaks, lower the frame rate to 30 fps for that scene. ## Features - The whole game and both DLC, from your own copy - Frame rates from 30 to 360 fps, or your display's own rate - Resolutions up to 4K and beyond, ultrawide, and FSR 1 upscaling - Graphics presets from Potato, below console quality, to Savage, far beyond it - Longer draw distance, sharper shadows, adjustable field of view, colour grading and HDR - Keyboard and mouse with real mouse camera, and any controller, gyro included - Button prompts that match your device - Save profiles, backups, and Wii U / Cemu save import - Steam Deck and PC handhelds - Photo mode, accessibility options and cheats ## Get started **You need:** your own game files (see [Game files](docs/game-files.md)), Windows 10 or later or Linux on x86-64, a GPU with Vulkan 1.3, 16 GB of RAM, a CPU with SSE4.2 (AVX2 runs faster) and about 20 GB of free disk space. 1. Download the latest build from [Releases](https://github.com/Revivedx/SavageWindRecomp/releases/latest): - **Windows:** the file ending in `windows.zip`. Extract it to a folder you can write to, not Program Files. - **Linux and Steam Deck:** the file ending in `x86_64.AppImage`. Make it executable and run it ([docs/linux.md](docs/linux.md)). - **Linux on ARM:** the file ending in `aarch64.AppImage`. It is highly experimental. 2. Start it and choose the folder with your extracted game (`exefs/` and `romfs/`). Then choose **Set up game files**. It checks the version, copies the files and recompiles the game code once, about 15 minutes on a 12-thread CPU. Your own files aren't changed. 3. Play. Settings and languages are in the game's Options. **Savage Wind Configuration** has your game files and the rest of the settings. **Updating:** from version 0.5.1 on, Savage Wind Configuration updates it in one click, on Windows and in the Linux AppImages. Before that, extract the new zip over the old folder or use the new AppImage. Your game files, saves and settings stay. Something wrong? See the [FAQ](docs/FAQ.md), which also lists the known issues. ## Saves Saves are in the `save` folder of Savage Wind's data folder: next to `savagewind.exe` on Windows, and in `~/.local/share/savagewind/save/` on Linux and the Steam Deck. To back them up or move them, close the game and copy the whole folder. More in [Saves](docs/saves.md), including profiles and Wii U / Cemu import. ## Status | Area | Share | Progress | |---|---|---| | Core game | 45% | ![Core game](docs/media/progress/area-core-game.svg) | | Platforms and input | 15% | ![Platforms and input](docs/media/progress/area-platforms-and-input.svg) | | Performance | 15% | ![Performance](docs/media/progress/area-performance.svg) | | Graphics options | 12% | ![Graphics options](docs/media/progress/area-graphics-options.svg) | | Player features | 13% | ![Player features](docs/media/progress/area-player-features.svg) | Every part, what it means and how the average is calculated: [Status](docs/STATUS.md). ## Controls Any controller SDL knows works. Keyboard and mouse defaults: | Action | Key | Action | Key | |---|---|---|---| | Move | W A S D | Camera | Mouse | | Jump | Space | Sprint / back | Left Shift | | Interact | E | Attack | Left click | | Shield | Right click | Bow | F | | Rune | Q | Throw | R | | Inventory | Tab | Map | M | Every action can be rebound in the game's Options. All the keys: [Controls](docs/controls.md). ## Found a bug? Read the [FAQ](docs/FAQ.md) first: issues about something it already covers are closed right away. Use the latest release and game version 1.9.0, search the [existing issues](https://github.com/Revivedx/SavageWindRecomp/issues?q=is%3Aissue), and [open one](https://github.com/Revivedx/SavageWindRecomp/issues/new/choose) with your `savagewind.log`. On a crash or a cutscene bug, attach your zipped `save` folder too. Reports without these are closed after 7 days. ## Contributing and building Open pull requests against the [`test`](https://github.com/Revivedx/SavageWindRecomp/tree/test) branch, which has everything ahead of the latest release. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). To build from source: [Windows](docs/BUILD-windows.md) and [Linux](docs/linux.md). ## Respect copyright - *The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild* is © Nintendo. This is a fan project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Nintendo. *Nintendo Switch* and *The Legend of Zelda* are trademarks of Nintendo. - This repository contains no game files, no game code (also not the C code the recompiler generates from it), no assets, no fonts, no keys - and release builds won't either. - The game code you generate and the build made from it contain Nintendo's code. They are for your own use only: don't share them, upload them or ship them. - Issues, pull requests or discussions that contain game files, keys, generated code or links to pirated copies will be removed. Piracy is not supported in any way. - Follow the copyright laws of your country. Dumping a game you own for personal use is legal in some countries and not in others; that is your responsibility. ## Credits and license Built on **[LAS Recomp](https://github.com/peiikai/LASRecomp)** by peiikai (MIT), with [TotK Recomp](https://github.com/valentderah/totk-pc-recomp) by Valiantsin Dzerakh (MIT) and [Ryujinx](https://github.com/Ryujinx/Ryujinx) (MIT) as references. Full list and the licenses of what releases bundle: [Credits](docs/third-party.md). Savage Wind Recomp's own code is under the [MIT License](LICENSE). The license covers this project's code only: it grants nothing for Nintendo's game, which you must supply yourself.
